chapter: Europe tours, Birdland memories and closing
title: Dinah Washington's respect for her mother, Ms. Jones
summary: Cobb says Dinah, born Ruth Jones, bought her mother a home and a car for her stepfather but would only be meek around her mother.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Dinah was beautiful. She took care of her mother. She bought her mother a home in Chicago and bought a car for her stepdaddy, Buick, and she was a lucky girl because she was good to her mother. She was good to her mother. And her mother was the only one that she wouldn't talk back to. She'd talk back to anybody but Ms. Jones. See, Dinah's real name was Ruth Jones. But Ms. Jones would take her back hand and clap her in the mouth if she said anything, and Dinah respected that woman. I was half scared of her myself.
: She had a big vocabulary. (inaudible) I know I heard her one --
I tell you one thing, she never used it with Ms. Jones.
I don't care how big it was. You've never seen Dinah so meek and humble in your life until she gets to Chicago around her mother.
Oh, sure, I love that respect. I love that respect. But anybody else, she'd blast off. Gladys Hampton did (inaudible) she didn't want to be there. She didn't want to hear Dinah put her mouth on.
